description:
Astralith 🚀 Forgotten by time, remembered among the stars.

We are a team of curious minds, creative thinkers, and space enthusiasts driven by a passion for exploration and storytelling. Through research, technology, creativity, and data, we aim to uncover the forgotten stories of abandoned human-made equipment on the Moon and Mars. We believe every forgotten machine holds a story worth telling. Join us to turn remnants of exploration into echoes that inspire the future!
summary:
We developed "Astralith: Abandoned, Not Forgotten", an interactive educational web application built with Next.js, TypeScript, and React that brings NASA’s legacy spacecraft across the Moon, Mars, and deep space to life for young explorers. The platform integrates six discovery modules: an interactive planetary landing map, a searchable Mission Explorer, an illustrated Story Reader, a side-by-side Mission Comparison tool, a student-friendly Space Glossary, and interactive STEM quizzes with progress tracking.

To address the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, we transformed dense NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) imagery, mission records, and landing coordinates into accessible, narrative-driven experiences tailored for school-age learners. Instead of static technical archives, students can pinpoint where historic rovers, landers, and probes rest and compare their engineering capabilities.

Over 60 years of pioneering space hardware sits silently beyond Earth, yet its stories are often hidden in complex telemetry. By connecting verified NASA open data with engaging, human-centered storytelling, our platform preserves spaceflight heritage and inspires the next generation of STEM explorers.
details:
Astralith: Abandoned, Not Forgotten is an interactive educational web platform that transforms over 60 years of NASA’s deactivated rovers, landers, and deep-space probes into engaging, narrative-driven learning experiences for young explorers. Users navigate through six integrated modules:

  • Planetary Map: An interactive surface viewer plotting exact landing and resting coordinates of legacy hardware across the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
  • Mission Explorer: A searchable, filterable directory of historic NASA missions featuring launch dates, destinations, scientific instruments, and mission status.
  • Story Reader: Illustrated, chapter-style mission narratives that recount each spacecraft’s journey, breakthroughs, and final resting place.
  • Mission Comparison: A side-by-side engineering benchmark tool where learners compare spacecraft mass, power sources, operational lifespans, and distances traveled.
  • Space Glossary: An accessible aerospace reference translating technical terms into clear, student-friendly language.
  • Knowledge Quizzes & Progress Tracking: Interactive quizzes paired with saved bookmarks and milestone tracking to reinforce comprehension.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Democratizing Space Archives: Raw telemetry and Planetary Data System (PDS) records are often inaccessible to K–12 students. Our platform translates complex engineering data into intuitive visual stories.
  • Preserving Spaceflight Heritage: By highlighting both famous icons and lesser-known surface hardware, the project honors the engineering milestones that paved the way for modern Artemis and Mars Sample Return missions.
  • Inspiring Future STEM Explorers: Combining spatial exploration, storytelling, and self-paced quizzes builds lasting curiosity and global space literacy among school-age learners and educators.

Tools, Languages & Data Used

  • Web Stack: Built with Next.js, React, and TypeScript, styled with modern responsive CSS for fast, interactive performance across desktop and tablet browsers.
  • NASA Open Data: Curated datasets structured from NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) imagery, NASA Science mission archives, and verified planetary landing coordinates.
  • Application Architecture: Modular client-side state management supporting instant mission filtering, side-by-side spec comparisons, and persistent learner progress/bookmarks.

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

  • Creative Approach: Rather than presenting retired spacecraft as static museum entries or spreadsheets, we give each machine a voice and geographic presence—allowing learners to "visit" where a rover rests on Mars, read its story, and immediately compare its capabilities against another mission.
    • Cognitive Load & Readability: Balanced rich historical detail with scannable layouts, clear visual hierarchy, and an embedded glossary so young learners never feel overwhelmed by jargon.
    • Scientific Accuracy: Every coordinate, timeline, and hardware specification is grounded in official NASA documentation.
    • Engagement & Replayability: Designed non-linear exploration paths—whether a student prefers maps, head-to-head stats, or quizzes—to support diverse learning styles.
